speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual start! Let's begin properly: how long have you had this painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and recent uveitis treatment, this lesion raises concern for an infectious or autoimmune etiology. Have you noticed any fever, chills, or swollen lymph nodes near the area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

The clinical presentation of a rapidly progressing, painful ulcer with a necrotic base and purplish borders, triggered by trauma (ant bite) in a patient with Crohn's disease and diabetes, is highly characteristic of Pyoderma Gangrenosum rather than an infectious etiology. I will not order further tests as the diagnosis is clinical; however, I recommend immediate wound protection and systemic immunosuppression.
